title: Paper Trail, Not Plaintext
description: A captain's logbook records that a crew member checked in, not the password they whispered at the gangplank. Register a fresh account and confirm what actually lands in the users table.
successCondition: Register a new account with a memorable password (e.g. "CorrectHorse1") via POST /api/auth/register. Query the users table directly with `npm run db:psql` and confirm the passwordHash column for that row is neither empty nor equal to the literal password string, and that login via POST /api/auth/login with the original password still succeeds afterward (proving the hash, not the raw password, is what's checked).
hints: passwordHash is produced with argon2 (see apps/api/src/modules/auth/service.ts) — it will look nothing like the input password, and won't be the same value between two accounts even with the same password.
select email, passwordHash from users where email = '<the email>'; is enough to eyeball the column directly.
